svg.title: When N is not a multiple of TILE
svg.text: When N is not a multiple of TILE
mm_tiled_1to1<2> on a 5 × 5 problem: grid round-up, zero padding, store guard, no early return
C index space covered by the grid: 3 × 3 blocks of 2 × 2 threads = 6 × 6 threads for a 5 × 5 C

g.text: N = 5 is not a multiple of TILE = 2. Grid = (5 + 1)/2 = 3 blocks per side, so 36 threads for 25 outputs.
(N + TILE − 1) / TILE rounds UP: no output is left without a thread.
The 11 threads marked × have row ≥ 5 or col ≥ 5: they own nothing.
They still exist, still load and still reach both barriers.
The K loop also rounds up: t = 0, 1, 2 covers k = 0…5, but k = 5 does not exist.
tiles along K: t = 0 → k 0–1, t = 1 → k 2–3, t = 2 → k 4–5
k = 5 is past the edge of A's columns and B's rows.
Block (2, 2) at t = 2: only thread (0,0) maps to real data. Every other load hits the guard and stores 0.0f.
block (2, 2), last step t = 2 (k = 4, 5):
sA
sB
thread (0,0): row 4, aCol 4 → A[4][4] ✓; bRow 4, col 4 → B[4][4] ✓
thread (1,0): col 5 ≥ N → sB = 0; aCol 5 ≥ N → sA = 0
thread (0,1): row 5 ≥ N → sA = 0; bRow 5 ≥ N → sB = 0
thread (1,1): everything out of range → 0, 0
Why zero is safe: the padding only ever multiplies into a sum. 0 × anything adds nothing.
block (2, 2), last step t = 2 (k = 4, 5):
sA
sB
thread (0,0), k = 0: A[4][4]·B[4][4] (real term)
so acc gets exactly the terms k = 0…4 ✓
the ternary (line 91–92) also stops OUT-OF-BOUNDS reads
Only the STORE is skipped (line 100). Threads never `return` early, because they must reach __syncthreads.
if (row < N && col < N) C[row*N + col] = acc; ← 1 of 4 threads stores
mm_naive uses an early return (line 48): fine there, it has no barrier.
A `return` in the tiled kernel would leave a barrier waiting for missing threads: undefined.
Cost: idle threads. Toy: 11 of 36 threads (31%) idle. At N = 32768 with TILE 32 or 64 there is NO waste.
32768 / 32 = 1024 and 32768 / 64 = 512 exactly: the measured sizes never hit the guards.
So the guards are correctness insurance, not a performance factor, in every benchmark run.
(At awkward small N they cost divergence in the last block row/column only.)
